The proposed design method achieves up to 78.3% reduction in cloak size compared to the original design.
A 71% reduction in normalized scattering cross section (SCS) at 10 GHz is demonstrated with the optimized cloak.
The cloak is based on quasi-conformal mapping (QCM) which allows isotropic refractive indices and broadband operation.
The approximated model replaces the diamond-shaped hidden object with a hexagonal object of reduced height and expanded width to better model anisotropy effects.
The refractive index profile is scaled by an optimal factor β to compensate for non-unity anisotropy and scattering by the hexagonal object.
The optimal scaling factor β for the approximated model is found to be 0.987 to minimize forward scattering.
The cloak maintains invisibility from 1 GHz to 26 GHz after optimal scaling, significantly broader than unscaled designs.
The anisotropy factor α in the original cloak design is approximately 1.044, indicating low but non-negligible anisotropy.
The refractive index profile is discretized into square unit cells of 2.45 mm size for fabrication.
The 3D-printed cloak material has a relative permittivity of 2.95 and dielectric loss tangent of 0.025 at 10 GHz.
Excessive size reduction leads to a loss of wave path control and increased anisotropy, degrading cloaking performance.
The normalized SCS of the cloak can be reduced from 0.888 (original) to 0.258 with size reduction and optimal scaling.
Full-wave simulations and experimental results show excellent agreement validating the approximated model.
The cloak is unidirectional due to the diamond-to-flat sheet transformation inherent in the QCM-based free-space cloak.
The method controls both the path and phase of electromagnetic waves by adjusting the refractive index gradient.
The refractive index below unity parts are approximated to free space (n=1) to ease fabrication constraints.
The cloak height was experimentally realized at 34 mm, limited by fabrication constraints on maximum refractive index.
The forward scattered power density is reduced by 75% after optimal scaling of the refractive index profile.
The cloak design uses slipping boundary conditions and modified Liao functional minimization for grid generation.
The scattering cross section is normalized by the total scattered power density with and without the cloak.
